factual_claims.source_evidence: Cash flow: 'Cash flow from ordinary operating activities of DKK -1.3M compared to negative DKK 4.3M in the same period last year... cash burn to net new ARR ratio of 0.9, which is in line with the level from year-end 2024.'

factual_claims.claim: SaaS metrics demonstrated strong product-market fit and customer retention.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Management commentary: 'Impero continued to demonstrate solid SaaS metrics, with an exceptionally low churn rate of 1% in 2025... We consider this as a testament to the value creation, product-market fit, and stickiness of our platform.'

factual_claims.claim: The churn rate remained exceptionally low at 1%, including zero churn within the DACH region, while the Net Revenue Retention Rate stabilized at 106%.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Financial highlights: 'Imperoʼs ARR growth rate of 19% YoY was in the upper end of the revised ARR growth range of 11–19%... with an exceptionally low churn rate of 1% in 2025... Net Revenue Retention Rate (NRR) ended at 106% in 2025.' Management commentary: 'In 2025, we had an exceptionally low churn rate of only 1%, including no churn across our customer base in the DACH region.'

factual_claims.claim: Average Revenue Per Account reached a record DKK 228 thousand, validating the land-and-expand strategy evidenced by a 12% gross uplift from the existing base.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: ARR development and SaaS metrics: 'We lifted the Average ARR per Account (ARPA) to a record high level of DKK 228T by the end of 2025... Net uplift of 7% was driven by a strong gross uplift to existing customers of DKK 4.5M, corresponding to 12%.'

factual_claims.claim: The customer roster surpassed 200 accounts, enhancing diversification as the proportion of ARR derived from the top ten customers decreased to 20% from 37% in 2020.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Management commentary: 'By the end of 2025, we reached a significant milestone as our customer base surpassed 200 customers... our top 10 customer concentration measured on ARR has decreased from 37% to 20% as of year-end 2025.'

factual_claims.claim: Revenue growth was concentrated in core regions, with net new ARR advancing 22% in Denmark and 26% in the DACH region, offsetting a 6% decline in other markets caused by substantial contract contractions in the UK totaling approximately DKK 1.8 million.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: ARR development: 'In Denmark, we increased net new ARR by a growth rate of 22% YoY... The DACH region led the growth with 26% growth YoY in 2025... ARR from other markets declined to DKK 5.5M by the end of the year, corresponding to -6% YoY in 2025, primarily explained by a larger contraction in the UK... totaling approx. DKK 1.0M in 2025.'

factual_claims.claim: The partner channel faced temporary delays in customer decision-making, limiting its contribution to new ARR generation in 2025, though network expansion in Germany positioned the company for future acceleration.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Management commentary: 'In 2025, our partners experienced delay in decision making from their customers, which dampened our partner sales in 2025... Importantly, our trusted partners are helping customers... In 2026 and onwards, we are continuously investing efforts to convert the existing and the new partner relationships into even closer cooperation... We are working with several certified consultancies across the German speaking markets, including the four leading global auditing networks (Big4) and have expanded to five revenue generating partners in the DACH region.'

factual_claims.claim: Following a successful private placement raising DKK 15 million in December 2025, the Board announced a strategic decision to defer the objective of achieving recurring positive cash flow before the end of 2026.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Strategy update: 'To strengthen the capital position... Impero successfully raised DKK 15M in a private placement in December 2025... With the improved capital position... the Board of Directors believes that growth investments will create more long-term value than pursuing a strategy of being cash flow positive on a recurring basis before the end of 2026. As a result, Impero has deferred its ambition of achieving positive cash flow on a recurring basis before the end of 2026... as announced in Company Announcement No. 3-2026.'

factual_claims.claim: This move prioritizes growth investments to capitalize on market opportunities, supported by an equity position of DKK 15.4 million and a cash balance of DKK 18.9 million.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Strategy update: 'As of 31 December 2025, Imperoʼs equity stood at DKK 15.4M... we entered 2026 with a solid cash position of DKK 18.9M... Financially, we are in a good position to invest prudently in commercial activities... We ended 2025 with a cash position of DKK 18.9M, with no interest-bearing debt.'

factual_claims.claim: Looking ahead to 2026, the company anticipates ARR growth of 15% to 23%, projecting ARR between DKK 53 million and DKK 57 million.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Guidance for 2026: 'By the end of 2026, Impero expects Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR) to reach between DKK 53M and 57M, corresponding to an ARR growth rate of approx. 15% to 23%.'

factual_claims.claim: The Board expects EBITDA to fluctuate between negative DKK 2 million and positive DKK 1 million, reflecting planned increases in commercial staffing and marketing expenditures, which are anticipated to have a delayed impact on revenue due to the length of enterprise sales cycles.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Guidance for 2026: 'For 2026, EBITDA is expected to be in the range of DKK -2M to +1M due to our planned acceleration of commercial investments... New planned hires across the commercial organization will increase the cost base, while having a limited short-term impact on ARR growth in 2026 due to onboarding ramp-up time and enterprise SaaS sales cycles.'
